Key Research Thinking Patterns: Data-Driven Correlation: Developing integrated databases to discover correlations between roadway characteristics and the occurrence of fatality collisions by translating data into a common format, merging databases based on geographical data, and analyzing the results to identify high-risk roadway sections (e.g., translating FARS and roadway characteristics/inventory data into a common format, using algorithms to translate location information between geographical location systems).

Hardware Context Switching: Designing low-overhead hardware context switching circuits to enable efficient thread migration between cores in a single-chip multiprocessor, reducing context switching latency and supporting multiple simultaneous thread switches (e.g., using a hardware context switching circuit to store the context of both currently running and time-multiplexed threads).

Real-Time Data Exchange: Developing vehicular networks using connected vehicles technology to increase driver safety by transmitting data packets to roadside units and displaying messages on display signs in real-time, based on information from neighboring vehicles (e.g., building an ad hoc network, implementing geographical routing, and developing algorithms to alert drivers of hazardous road conditions).

Multitasking Optimization: Developing algorithms and techniques to optimize multitasking, thread migration, fine-grained scheduling, and load balancing in high-performance computing systems, including asymmetric multi-core processors and memory-level-parallelism-targeted processors (e.g., using fine-grained scheduling to reduce pipeline stalls and cache misses)
Summary Description: Ronald Barnes is a researcher specializing in transportation engineering, data analysis, and computer science. His primary focus is on developing intelligent transportation systems (ITS) to improve roadway safety, highway planning, and traffic engineering. He employs data-driven correlation, hardware context switching, real-time data exchange, and multitasking optimization techniques to design and implement efficient and effective solutions. His work involves translating data into common formats, merging databases, and analyzing results to identify high-risk roadway sections. He also designs low-overhead hardware context switching circuits and develops vehicular networks using connected vehicles technology to increase driver safety. His research has significant implications for transportation systems, power management, and performance optimization.
